uncited: Gaussian and Primitive Splatting methods represent 3D scenes as a collection of parameterized volumetric primitives (typically Gaussians or neural-defined kernels) that are rasterized or splatted onto the image plane, offering a trade-off between the expressivity of neural implicit fields and the rendering speed of explicit primitives.
Rendering involves sampling points along a ray.

This model is physically based on light propagation from one point $\mathbf{r}(t_0)$ to another $\mathbf{r}(t)$ along a ray with origin $\mathbf{o}$ and direction $\mathbf{d}$, where $\sigma(\mathbf{p})$ denotes density.
